353252.title: SE(s) extremal conjecture for weighted Laplacian spread
353252.review_depth: Literal statement; Barrett-Evans-Hall-Kempton arXiv:2201.04225v1 Section 4.3 (Definition 4.7, Theorem 4.8, Conjecture 6) read.
353252.mechanism_and_prior_art: Random-restart local search over weights in [0,1] converges to x+y-2xy/n = 1 exactly (SE(s) family), never below. Counterexample would be Lean-cheap (rational Rayleigh-quotient upper bounds on lambda_2 of G and G^c plus monotonicity), but none found. A proof needs a strengthened weighted Laplacian-spread argument (u*v <= n(n-2)/4 with u = n/2 - lambda_2, v = lambda_n - n/2), beyond the spread bound (n-1).
353252.finite_search_coverage: n=5: 20 restarts x 1500 steps; n=6: 12 restarts x 1200 steps; minimum 1 - 1e-14 (equality family).

382049.title: The chordal graph representation conjecture for clique and reduced clique graphs
382049.review_depth: Literal statement; Mayhew-Probert arXiv:2301.03781v4 Sections 3-4 (Theorem 3.2, Conjectures 4.1-4.3) read.
382049.mechanism_and_prior_art: Conjecture 4.2 claims every chordal H is C(G) for a chordal G. By the source's own printed Theorem 3.2 (Szwarcfiter-Bornstein) and the classical identity K(chordal) = dually chordal (Brandstaedt-Dragan-Chepoi-Voloshin 1998), the 3-sun (chordal, not dually chordal) is not C(G). Exhaustive check: of the 58 connected chordal graphs on 6 vertices exactly one (the 3-sun) fails Theorem 3.2. A smallest classical example plus a printed source theorem: zero credit.

382066.title: The strongly chordal graph conjecture for graphic arrangements
382066.review_depth: Literal statement; arXiv:2302.00343v1 Definition 1.1, Section 6 (Theorem 6.4, Remark 6.7, Prop 6.10, Thm 6.12, Thm 6.16, Def 6.17, Thm 6.19, Conjecture 6.20) read. Web search: no later resolution found.
382066.mechanism_and_prior_art: Exact combinatorial reformulation: A_G flag-accurate iff a contraction sequence exists whose simple quotients are chordal with exponents (PEO earlier-neighbour counts) equal to the initial segments of exp(A_G) (Stanley/Edelman-Reiner freeness = chordality; restriction = contraction). Partial proof route: contracting an edge at a simplicial vertex u deletes u and removes exponent deg(u), and max exponent = omega-1, so repeated deletion of simplicial vertices lying in maximum cliques suffices; by hand this fails for the strongly chordal Q_4 with outer triangles on edges 01, 02, 03 (no simplicial vertex in its unique K_4), which the search nevertheless finds flag-accurate via other contractions. No general proof found.
382066.finite_search_coverage: ALL connected strongly chordal graphs up to isomorphism: n<=9 (1,2,5,15,57,263,1497,10278) and every one-vertex clique extension of all 10278 graphs on 9 vertices (all connected strongly chordal graphs on 10 vertices; 8 chunks, ~245k chunk-level checks): no graph fails flag-accuracy. Controls: source Prop. 6.10 graphs Q_4(1^6), Q_4(2^6) detected as NOT flag-accurate; 3-sun flag-accurate (Cor. 6.9).
382066.remaining_lemmas_or_notes: A counterexample would need Terao factorisation / freeness theory in Lean (absent from mathlib); a proof would need the same. Next lemma to try (unchecked): every connected strongly chordal graph has an edge whose contraction is chordal, removes exactly one maximal exponent, and stays strongly chordal; that would give a proof by induction.
